source_refs.note: Exercise 14.3, Question 13: moment about M(1, -3, 3) of the force AB, r = MA (book p.283). Answer key PDF 312: 48i - 4j + 30k.

blocks.prompt: 13. Find the moment about the point \(M(1, -3, 3)\) of the force represented by \(\underline{AB}\), where the coordinates of points \(A(4, 3, -1)\) and \(B(-1, 3, 7)\) are given.
blocks.explanation:
A moment-of-force question.
We must find the moment (a vector) of \(\underline{F}\) about \(M\).
Plan: \(\underline{r} = \underline{MA}\), then \(\underline{r} \times \underline{F}\) by the determinant.
steps:
Given: force \(\underline{F}\) acting through \(A(4, 3, -1)\); point \(M(1, -3, 3)\).
To find: the moment of \(\underline{F}\) about \(M\).
Method: Moment \(= \underline{r} \times \underline{F}\) (14.3.7 (c)), where \(\underline{r}\) is the vector from the point \(M\) (about which we turn) to a point \(A\) on the line of action of the force. The force is represented by \(\underline{AB}\), so \(\underline{F} = \underline{AB}\) = (position of \(B\)) minus (position of \(A\)).

Write the force
\[\underline{F} = \underline{AB} = (-1 - 4)\underline{i} + (3 - 3)\underline{j} + (7 - (-1))\underline{k}\]
\[= -5\underline{i} + 8\underline{k}\]
Why: A vector from \(A\) to \(B\) is (end) minus (start).

Find \(\underline{r} = \underline{MA}\)
\[\underline{MA} = (4 - 1)\underline{i} + (3 - (-3))\underline{j} + (-1 - 3)\underline{k}\]
\[= 3\underline{i} + 6\underline{j} - 4\underline{k}\]
Why: \(\underline{r}\) starts at the point \(M\) about which the moment is taken and ends at the point \(A\) where the force acts.

Write the determinant
\[\underline{r} \times \underline{F} = \begin{vmatrix} \underline{i} & \underline{j} & \underline{k} \\ 3 & 6 & -4 \\ -5 & 0 & 8 \end{vmatrix}\]
Why: Row 1 holds the unit vectors, row 2 the components of the first vector \(\underline{r}\), row 3 those of the second \(\underline{F}\). The order of the rows follows the order of the product.

Work out the three minors
\[\underline{i}\text{ minor} = (6)(8) - (-4)(0) = 48\]
\[\underline{j}\text{ minor} = (3)(8) - (-4)(-5) = 4\]
\[\underline{k}\text{ minor} = (3)(0) - (6)(-5) = 30\]
Why: For each unit vector cover its row and column; the minor is (top-left)(bottom-right) minus (top-right)(bottom-left).

Attach the signs \(+, -, +\)
\[\underline{r} \times \underline{F} = \underline{i}(48) - \underline{j}(4) + \underline{k}(30)\]
\[= 48\underline{i} - 4\underline{j} + 30\underline{k}\]
Why: Expanding a determinant along row 1 uses the sign pattern \(+, -, +\); the middle (\(\underline{j}\)) term is subtracted.

Magnitude of the moment
\[|\underline{r} \times \underline{F}| = \sqrt{(48)^2 + (-4)^2 + (30)^2}\]
\[= \sqrt{3220} = 2 \sqrt{805}\]
Why: The length tells how strong the turning effect is.

Check
\[(\underline{r} \times \underline{F}) \cdot \underline{F} = (48)(-5) + (-4)(0) + (30)(8)\]
\[= -240 + 0 + 240 = 0\]
Why: The moment \(\underline{r} \times \underline{F}\) must be perpendicular to \(\underline{F}\) (and to \(\underline{r}\)); the dot product is 0.
